subtitle: How a Fallen Capital Could Not Silence a Line of Kings

panels.shot: wide, moody three-quarter view of an aged king and two younger princes against a fading palace skyline and a misty river delta
panels.action: Lakshmanasena stands in worn but regal robes beside the younger Vishvarupasena and Keshavasena, a copper-plate grant held between them, as the towers of Nabadwip blur behind and the waterways of eastern Bengal stretch ahead under a dimming sky.

dialogue.text: The chronicles remember Lakshmanasena fleeing Nabadwip; the copper plates whisper another tale — of kings who lost a capital but kept a crown alive in the marshy east.

i18n.hi: कथाएँ कहती हैं लक्ष्मणसेन नवद्वीप से भागे; मगर ताम्रपत्र फुसफुसाते हैं दूसरी दास्तान — राजधानी खोकर भी दलदली पूरब में ताज बचाए राजाओं की।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an aged Lakshmanasena seated in a lamplit hall, scrolls and poets around him
panels.action: Lakshmanasena, white-bearded yet upright, sits on a low throne in his Nabadwip court, palm-leaf manuscripts piled nearby as court scholars and poets gesture over verses in the warm glow of oil lamps.

dialogue.text: Before the raid, Lakshmanasena ruled from Nabadwip, where Sanskrit verses, legal digests and songs like Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda flowed through a court that thought its order would last.

i18n.hi: हमले से पहले लक्ष्मणसेन नवद्वीप से राज करते थे; जहाँ संस्कृत काव्य, विधि-संग्रह और जयदेव के गीत गोविंद जैसे गान बहते थे, एक ऐसे दरबार में जिसे अपना क़ायदा सदियों का लगा।

panels.shot: overhead wide of Nabadwip’s riverfront and palace, with distant riders at the horizon
panels.action: From above, the palace and temples of Nabadwip line the riverbank as boats move slowly along the water, while far off on the dusty horizon a small band of riders pushes hard toward the city.

dialogue.text: Around 1203–1204, from the Ghurid frontier, Ikhtiyar al-Din Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji drove hard into this world with a fast raid that the Persian chronicler Minhaj-i-Siraj would later describe in sharp, breathless lines.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1203–1204 में ग़ोरी सरहद से इख़्तियार अल-दीन मुहम्मद बख्तियार ख़िलजी घोड़े की रफ़्तार से इस दुनिया पर टूटा; जिसे फ़ारसी इतिहासकार मिन्हाज-ए-सिराज ने बाद में तेज़, हाँफती पंक्तियों में लिखा।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a riverside pavilion, Lakshmanasena turning toward commotion beyond the columns
panels.action: Inside a river-facing pavilion, Lakshmanasena rises from a cushioned seat, startled, as courtiers rush in and point toward unseen turmoil in the city streets beyond the carved stone pillars.

dialogue.text: Minhaj does not paint a long battle. He tells of a sudden strike, of the aged Lakshmanasena taken unawares in his capital, and of a decision made in moments — to stand, or to slip away and live.

i18n.hi: मिन्हाज कोई लंबी जंग नहीं दिखाता। वह अचानक धावे की कहानी कहता है — बुज़ुर्ग लक्ष्मणसेन राजधानी में ही गाफ़िल पकड़े गए, और पलों में ही फ़ैसला करना पड़ा — डटे रहें या फिसल कर जान बचाएँ।

panels.shot: low-angle view from inside a crowded boat as Lakshmanasena steps in, city receding
panels.action: Seen from within a rocking boat, Lakshmanasena steps carefully aboard with the help of attendants, his face lined with strain, while behind him the outline of Nabadwip’s palaces and temple spires grows small along the riverbank.

dialogue.text: The chronicler writes that the old king fled by boat, leaving Nabadwip to the raiders. To later readers, it looked like an ending. Yet the river did not carry him out of history.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार लिखता है कि बूढ़ा राजा नाव से भाग निकला, नवद्वीप लुटेरों पर छोड़कर। बाद के पाठकों को यह अंत लगा। पर नदी उसे इतिहास से बहाकर न ले जा सकी।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye blending into landscape, tracing a boat’s path eastward along branching rivers
panels.action: A stylized view shows a slender royal boat gliding along a braided river system, the lush, watery plains of eastern Bengal unfolding beneath like a living map of channels, marshes and scattered hamlets.

dialogue.text: The Ganga delta opened eastwards into Vanga and Vikrampura — a land of rivers, paddy and scattered power. Here, away from the fallen western capital, the Senas began to root their next act.

i18n.hi: गंगा डेल्टा पूरब में वंग और विक्रमपुर की ओर खुलता था — नदियों, धान और बिखरी ताक़तों की धरती। यहीं, गिरी पश्चिमी राजधानी से दूर, सेनाओं ने अपनी अगली कहानी जमानी शुरू की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Lakshmanasena in a simpler hall in Vikrampura, in counsel with his sons
panels.action: In a more modest hall at Vikrampura, Lakshmanasena sits on a low platform with maps and copper plates laid out, speaking gravely to the younger Vishvarupasena and Keshavasena who kneel before him in attentive resolve.

dialogue.speaker: Lakshmanasena
dialogue.text: The west is gone, my sons. But a king’s duty runs where his people still stand.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम चला गया, बेटों। पर राजधर्म वहाँ तक चलता है, जहाँ तक हमारे लोग खड़े हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on hands engraving a copper plate, sparks of metal dust catching the lamplight
panels.action: A craftsman’s steady hands incise precise Nagari letters into a gleaming copper plate, while Lakshmanasena and Vishvarupasena watch in the background, their faces lit by the glow of the oil lamp reflecting off the metal.

dialogue.text: Their weapons now were words in metal. Copper plates, with seals and formulas, carried the king’s will into the fields, forests and monasteries of eastern Bengal.

i18n.hi: अब उनके हथियार शब्द थे, धातु पर उकेरे हुए। मुहरों और फ़ार्मूलों वाले ताम्रपत्रों ने राजा की मर्ज़ी को पूरबी बंगाल के खेतों, जंगलों और मठों तक पहुँचा दिया।

panels.shot: insert-style shot of a finished plate on a cloth, its inscription and royal seal prominent
panels.action: A newly finished copper plate rests on a folded cloth, its polished surface inscribed with neat lines of Sanskrit, a lion-emblem seal stamped proudly near the top, while a royal messenger’s hand reaches in to lift it.

dialogue.text: Later, the Madanpara copper plate would preserve the name of Vishvarupasena, king in Vikrampura, granting lands with the old Sena titles even after Nabadwip had slipped from their hands.

i18n.hi: बाद में मदनपाड़ा का ताम्रपत्र विश्वरूपसेन का नाम बचाए रखेगा — विक्रमपुर का राजा, जो नवद्वीप हाथ से निकल जाने पर भी पुरानी सेना उपाधियों के साथ ज़मीनें बाँट रहा था।

panels.shot: wide rural shot of a grantee receiving the plate in a village clearing, with river and fields behind
panels.action: In a village clearing beside ripening paddy and a slow river, a Brahmin elder with shaven head and sacred thread bows as a royal officer hands him the shining copper plate, while villagers watch from a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: These grants tied local landholders, Brahmins and religious houses to a court now anchored in the east. The form of rule remained familiar: gifts of land in return for loyalty, ritual and memory.

i18n.hi: इन दानों ने स्थानीय ज़मींदारों, ब्राह्मणों और मठों को अब पूरब में जमे दरबार से जोड़ दिया। राज चलाने की शक्ल वही रही — वफ़ादारी, पूजा और याद के बदले ज़मीन की बख़्शीश।

panels.shot: contrast shot split subtly: on one side a bustling Lakhnauti, on the other the quieter Vikrampura court
panels.action: The frame balances two scenes: to one side, the busy walls and markets of Lakhnauti under new Muslim officials; to the other, the smaller but orderly court of Vikrampura where Vishvarupasena consults a copper plate with advisers.

dialogue.text: To the west, Bakhtiyar’s successors centred power at Lakhnauti under Ghurid and then Delhi authority. To the east, the Sena court shrank yet survived, one polity among many on a changing frontier.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में बख्तियार के वारिसों ने लखनौती में शक्ति का सेंटर बनाया, पहले ग़ोरी, फिर दिल्ली सल्तनत के तहत। पूरब में सेना दरबार सिमट गया, पर बचा रहा — बदलती सरहद पर बस एक और रियासत बनकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of a poet reciting before Vishvarupasena, with musicians behind
panels.action: In a candlelit hall, a court poet with palm-leaf manuscript raises his hand mid-recitation before Vishvarupasena, who listens intently, while veena and drum players sit ready, evoking the older Nabadwip courtly culture.

dialogue.text: Even as politics shifted, echoes of Lakshmanasena’s old court lived on. Poets still sang Krishna’s love in refined Sanskrit metres, jurists still copied digests, the Sena social order still shaped gifts and honours.

i18n.hi: सियासत बदलती रही, पर लक्ष्मणसेन के पुराने दरबार की गूंज जीवित रही। कवि अब भी संस्कृत छंदों में कृष्ण प्रेम गाते, विधिवेत्ता अब भी ग्रंथ नकल करते, सेना का सामाजिक ढाँचा अब भी दान और सम्मान तय करता।

panels.shot: close-up of an aging Vishvarupasena handing a royal insignia to a younger Keshavasena
panels.action: An older Vishvarupasena, his hair streaked with grey, clasps Keshavasena’s shoulder and presses a small royal emblem into his hand, their eyes meeting in a heavy, unspoken transfer of burden.

dialogue.speaker: Vishvarupasena
dialogue.text: Hold what you can, where you can. A smaller realm is still a realm.

i18n.hi: जितना बचा सको, उतना थामे रहो। छोटा राज्य भी, राज्य ही होता है।

panels.shot: insert close-up of the Edilpur/Adilpur copper plate being unrolled and examined by later hands
panels.action: Centuries later, in a dim archive, a scholar’s hands unroll a rubbing of the Edilpur copper plate, the engraved name of Keshavasena clearly visible among the script lines as dust motes drift in the light.

dialogue.text: The Edilpur copper plate bears Keshavasena’s name. It shows that, for decades after Nabadwip’s fall, the Sena lineage still issued grants, still claimed kingship from their eastern base.

i18n.hi: एदिलपुर ताम्रपत्र पर केशवसेन का नाम दर्ज है। यह दिखाता है कि नवद्वीप के गिरने के दशकों बाद तक, सेना वंश ताम्रपत्र निकालता रहा, और अपने पूरबी गढ़ से राज-पद का दावा करता रहा।

panels.shot: wide, atmospheric shot of a misty Vikrampura landscape with crumbling structures and boats moving on
panels.action: Under a pale morning mist, the remains of Sena-era brick walls and mounds rise beside a quiet river at Vikrampura, while small boats glide past and farmers work the fields, life continuing around the fading ruins.

dialogue.text: In time, the Sena name faded from active politics. Other chiefs rose in eastern Bengal; the delta’s wet fields drew new settlers and new alliances under later regimes.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ सेना नाम सक्रिय सियासत से धुँधला गया। पूरबी बंगाल में नए सरदार उठे; डेल्टा के गीले खेतों ने नए बसने वाले और नई गँठजोड़ें खींचीं, बाद की सल्तनतों के साये में।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern archaeologist or historian in the field, holding a plate impression against the landscape
panels.action: A modern researcher stands amid grassy mounds at a Vikrampura site, holding up an inked impression of a copper plate toward the horizon, aligning its text with the land and rivers spread before him.

dialogue.text: Modern historians, reading Minhaj’s chronicle alongside these plates, see not a sudden erasure but a slow redrawing of maps — with overlapping sovereignties stretching across the moist edge of the delta.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार, मिन्हाज की तारीख़ को इन ताम्रपत्रों के साथ पढ़कर, अचानक मिटा देना नहीं, बल्कि नक्शों का धीरे-धीरे फिर से बनना देखते हैं — आपस में घुली कई हकूमतें, जो डेल्टा के गीले किनारों पर पसरी थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on the faces of Lakshmanasena, Vishvarupasena and Keshavasena in a ghostly montage over river currents
panels.action: The solemn faces of Lakshmanasena, Vishvarupasena and Keshavasena appear as a translucent montage above swirling river currents, their expressions calm yet unyielding, as if watching the centuries pass below.

dialogue.text: Their story shows how a dynasty can lose its proudest city yet linger in the margins, on metal and in memory — reminding us that the fall of a capital is not always the end of a line.

i18n.hi: उनकी दास्तान दिखाती है कि एक वंश अपना शानदार शहर खोकर भी हाशियों में जी सकता है — धातु पर खुदा, और ज़हन में जीवित — याद दिलाते हुए कि राजधानी का पतन, वंश की आख़िरी साँस ज़रूरी नहीं होता।

title_i18n.en: The Last Sena Kings of Vikrampura

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Fallen Capital Could Not Silence a Line of Kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: गिरा हुआ राजधानी, पर ख़ामोश न हुई राजाओं की लड़ी
